name: Instapage
summary: Enterprise landing-page and conversion platform: build, personalize and A/B-test post-click landing pages at scale, with ad-to-page mapping, heatmaps and fast AMP pages. Built for paid-ads and demand-gen teams.
best_for: marketing teams running significant paid ad campaigns who need post-click optimisation: AdMap ad-to-page personalisation, A/B testing and heatmaps
skip_if: you run limited ad campaigns or want budget pricing: at $99+/mo it's overkill below real paid-traffic volume
honest_knock: It's premium-priced and only justified by serious ad spend: Create is $79 a month billed annually for 15,000 unique monthly visitors, and the price per thousand barely improves as you climb, so the higher tiers buy features rather than cheaper traffic. The 14-day trial needs a card and carries its own cap of 2,500 visitors; crossing it ends the trial and starts the paid plan by itself. And there's the ownership question the feature list does not raise: publishing to your own domain means pointing a CNAME at Instapage, their help centre carries a per-registrar guide for exactly that, so the page is served by them and lives as long as the subscription does. Their own docs add a second catch worth knowing before you standardise on it: “we lock domains under the first Instapage account that uses them”. Treat these pages as rented campaign infrastructure, not as part of your site, and keep the copy somewhere you control.

pricing.entry_price_terms: per month billed yearly ($99 month to month) for 15,000 visitors
pricing.notes: (re-verified 27 Nov 2026; amounts unchanged since 4 Sep) Instapage does publish plan prices; they are not on the URL we had recorded. instapage.com/en/pricing redirects to the homepage at instapage.com/lp, and the plan table sits at instapage.com/plans. Our 26 August reading landed on the redirect, found no figures and concluded that prices had been withdrawn; the figures below match the last published rates this dossier already held, so the more likely explanation is a moved page rather than a withdrawal. Three tiers sit there. Create is $99 a month month-to-month or $79 billed annually, for 15,000 unique monthly visitors. Optimize is $199 or $159 annually for 30,000 unique monthly visitors, with selectors for 50,000 and for a custom volume — the custom option defaults to 50,000 and hands you to sales. Convert is quote-only. Annual billing is advertised as 'save up to 20%', and every tier carries unlimited contacts. The 14-day free trial asks for a credit card and is capped at 2,500 unique monthly visitors; Instapage's own FAQ states that exceeding that cap ends the trial automatically and moves you onto the paid plan you selected. The comparison table on the same page lists 10 team members on every self-serve column; 2 subdomains and 1 workspace on both Create and the 30,000-visitor Optimize, rising to 10 subdomains and 5 workspaces at 50,000 visitors; and 15, 30 and 50 pages per Collection. Publishing to the root domain (yoursite.com) is listed only under Convert. The FAQ says custom usage is not offered below the 50,000-visitor Optimize option. The FAQ read 27 November 2026 adds that custom limits are currently available with annual contracts only. The comparison table also meters email and API use: 15,000 email sends a month (1,500 a day) and 5,000 API calls a day on Create, 30,000 (3,000 a day) and 10,000 on the 30,000-visitor Optimize, and 50,000 (5,000 a day) and 15,000 at 50,000 visitors. A fourth column at 100,000 visitors carries 100,000 sends and 30,000 API calls a day, but the plain page text does not name its plan, so we do not assign it to one.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 19 November 2026 the session tested Instapage in the 14-day Create trial that we started with our card. Editing a template page and adding a form worked in a few minutes, and the AI generator made two versions in about 5 minutes. Experiment, Personalize and AdMap are locked on Create. The trial is set to bill $948 for a year on 3 December; cancelling took three clicks with no retention offer. Account and start: we created the account on the Create plan and started the 14-day trial with his own card; our AI assistant ran the test in our browser, in its own tab, on 19 November 2026 from 13:07. The interface was in English. Subscription showed Plan: Create (14-days free trial), Annual Payment: $948 and First billing date: 3 DEC 2026, with trial limits of 0 / 2500 visitors, 10 team members, 1 workspace, 2 subdomains, 3 e-mails a day and 8 AI page generations a month. Core action, a landing page: from the dashboard, Create a page showed 294 Layouts; the DriveOn template opened in the editor after about 15 seconds (13:09), 4 clicks from the dashboard. The headline was changed to Test Project: Drive Your Way, which worked. From the Forms library the template Detailed Email Sign Up (Name, Email) was inserted; it landed on top of the logo and would have to be moved. SAVE AS GLOBAL FORM is a paid feature. The page was saved as a draft and not published. The preview opened in its own tab with the changes. The AI generator (BETA, 8 generations left, at least 30 characters) got a one-line prompt for a car sharing page at 13:10 and showed two versions after about 5 minutes (13:15); neither was kept. Plans: Experiment shows only an introduction with plans and pricing, Personalize says To start personalizing, you need to upgrade to our Convert plan, and AdMap asks for an upgrade; both go to sales. The dossier gives Create at $79 a month billed annually, which matches the Annual Payment of $948. Checkout: the trial checkout was done by us before the session and was not seen. Cancelling, done the same day: avatar, My Account Admin, Subscription, CANCEL ACCOUNT. Step 1 asks for reasons (we chose Other and typed Just testing); step 2 says that after the 14 day trial all live pages will be unpublished and that the account stays free to build pages, with CANCEL ACCOUNT. No retention offer, no discount, no pause and no password. After the final click (19 November 2026, 12:35 UTC) the app said Cancellation Successful. After a reload Subscription said Your plan will cancel at the end of the billing cycle, with access to the plan features until 3 DEC 2026 12:03:02, and First billing date: N/A, so the $948 charge is stopped. Three clicks from the subscription page. Not tested: publishing, a subdomain or own domain, integrations, an A/B test, Personalize and AdMap, the mobile editor, contacts, e-mails and analytics. Clean up: the account and the draft page stay; the tab with the AI versions could not be closed because the page asked to confirm leaving. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: An inserted form lands on top of the page and has to be moved by hand. The trial is set to bill a full year, $948, on 3 December. After cancelling, live pages are unpublished when the trial ends.
